Content

  1. 2. Semiconductors: Materials with conductivity values between conductors and insulators, offering the possibility to control their conductivity. E.g. Silicon, germanium, and various compounds like arsenide.
  1. 3. Insulators: Materials that resist the flow of electric current, having high electrical resistivity and low conductivity. E.g. Rubber, glass, plastic, air, pure water.

Resistance Combination

  • In electrical circuits, resistors can be connected in two primary ways: Series and Parallel.

#### Series Connection

  • In a series circuit, resistors are connected end-to-end, forming a single path for current flow.
  • Current (I) is the same through each resistor.
  • Voltage (V) is divided across each resistor depending on its resistance.

R_eq = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + ... + Rₙ

  • Where, R₁, R₂, R₃ ... Rₙ are individual resistor value.
  • Same current, different potential difference.

#### Parallel Connection

  • In a parallel circuit, resistors are connected across the same two points, creating multiple paths for current flow.
  • Voltage (V) is the same across each resistor.
  • Current (I) is divided based on the resistance of each branch.

1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃ + ... + 1/Rₙ

  • Same potential difference, different current.
  • Appliances in our home are connected in Parallel Connection.

Questionnaire: Two resistors of 20Ω and 4Ω respectively are connected in series connection to a 6V battery, what is the current flow?

Sol: Given

  • R₁ = 20Ω
  • R₂ = 4Ω
  • Voltage of the battery (V) = 6V
  • Connection = Series

In a series connection:

  • R_total = R₁ + R₂ = 20Ω + 4Ω = 24Ω
  • I = V / R
  • I = 6V / 24Ω
  • I = 0.25 A

Questionnaire: Three resistors of 5Ω, 10Ω, and 30Ω respectively are connected in parallel connection with a potential difference of 12V, what is the current flow?

Sol: Given

  • R₁ = 5Ω
  • R₂ = 10Ω
  • R₃ = 30Ω
  • Voltage across each resistor (V) = 12V
  • Connection = Parallel

In a parallel connection:

  • 1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃
  • 1/R_eq = 1/5 + 1/10 + 1/30
  • 1/R_eq = (6 + 3 + 1) / 30
  • R_eq = 3Ω
  • V = IR
  • 12 = I × 3
  • I = 4 A

Heating Effect of Electric Current

  • When an electric current flows through a conductor, it produces heat due to the resistance of the conductor. This phenomenon is called the heating effect of electric current.

Joule's Law of Heating

  • The heat produced in a resistor due to the flow of current is given by:

Heat (H) = I²Rt

Where:

  • H = Heat energy (in joules)
  • I = Current (in amperes)
  • R = Resistance (in ohms)
  • t = Time (in seconds)

Alternate Forms:

Using Ohm's Law (V = IR), the formula can also be written as:

H = VIt or H = V²t / R

Applications of Heating Effect of Electric Current

ApplicationDetails
Electric HeaterNichrome wire used as heating element
Electric bulbTungsten filament (high melting point)
Electric ironUses the heating effect to iron clothes
FuseThin wire with low melting point to protect appliances

Important Notes:

  • Nichrome is commonly used in heating devices because it has high resistance and it does not oxidize easily at high temperatures.
  • A fuse melts when excessive current flows, breaking the circuit and preventing damage. It is used to protect electrical appliances from excessive current and to prevent short circuits or mismatched loads.

Electric Power

Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or produced.

  • P = VI
  • P = I²R → (∵ V = IR)
  • P = V² / R

Where:

  • V = Voltage
  • I = Current
  • R = Resistance

Commercial Unit of Energy → kWh

  • 1 unit = 1kWh
  • 1 kWh = 1 kW × 1 hour = 1000 watts × 3600 secs
  • = 3,600,000 watt-seconds or joules
  • = 36 × 10⁵ Ws
  • = 3.6 × 10⁶ J

Colour Coding in Household Wiring

  • Live wire: Red (high voltage)
  • Neutral: Black (V = 0)
  • Ground/Earth: Green/Yellow
  • In electrical appliances: 220V; 50Hz

(Diagram: Earth wire is made thick such that it can manage higher currents with low resistance)

Wheatstone Bridge

  • A Wheatstone bridge is an electrical circuit used to accurately measure an unknown resistance by balancing two legs of a bridge circuit using 4 resistors.

P/R = Q/S

Questionnaire: Calculate the electrical energy consumed by a 1200 W toaster in 30 mins. What will be the cost of using the same for 1 month if 1 unit of electricity cost Rs. 4?

Sol: Given

  • Power of toaster = 1200 W = 1.2 kW
  • Time used = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours
  • Cost of 1 unit (1 kWh) = Rs. 4
  • Usage = 1 time/day for 30 days
  • Energy = Power × Time = 1.2 kW × 0.5 hr = 0.6 units (kWh)
  • Monthly Energy = 0.6 × 30 = 18 units
  • Cost = 18 × 4 = Rs. 72
  • Energy consumed per day = 0.6 units
  • Total energy for 30 days = 18 units
  • Cost for 1 month = Rs. 72

Kirchhoff's Law

  1. 1. Law of Current: It states that the total current entering a node (junction) in a circuit is equal to the total current leaving that node.

Σ I_in = Σ I_out

  1. 2. Law of Voltage: The sum of all voltages (EMFs and voltage drops) around any closed loop in a circuit is equal to zero (ΣV = 0).
